messages:
amy: Quick post-all-hands thread for folks who had Qs about appeals, band moves, and manager calibration. Drop anything we missed and I9ll follow up. :wave:

ravi: Thanks Amy. One ask from my director: if someone appeals a calibration outcome, what's the timeline and who reviews it?

amy: Good one. Appeals go to a small review panel (People Ops + 2 senior ICs from another org) and we aim for a 10-business-day turnaround. Managers should submit the appeal packet with supporting evidence (work examples, peer feedback, and any missed context). Appeals are not guaranteed to change outcomes but are reviewed for process errors or missed evidence.

zara: For band reassignments (e.g., moving someone to a new band due to scope change but not a title promo), is that handled in the same packet or separate?

amy: We treat band moves as comp actions and they can be submitted as part of the spring packet or via the off-cycle packet if urgent. Band-only moves still need manager rationale, examples of expanded scope, and recommended target comp within the new band. Finance will validate market positioning.

bryan: Eligibility question: if someone joined mid-cycle (joined March 20), are they included in promotion considerations this cycle or next?

amy: New hires are eligible for promotion after 6 months in role, unless the manager requests an early review with strong evidence. For mid-cycle joiners we generally advise waiting for the next formal cycle unless there's exceptional case for early consideration.

peopleops-bot: Posted canonical timeline: https://redwood.internal/hr/reviews/2026-spring (internal only). Attachment: "Manager checklist, appeal form, off-cycle template." :link:

amy: Also clarifying appeals process steps for managers: 1) Submit appeal packet within 5 business days after manager 1:1s complete; 2) Panel review (~10 business days); 3) Outcome communicated and payroll adjustments if any. I'll paste the short checklist below.

amy: ```
Appeal checklist (manager-submitted):
- Employee name + current role/band
- Reason for appeal + timeline of missed context
- 3-4 supporting work examples (links)
- Peer/PM feedback excerpts
- Manager recommendations (desired outcome)
```

ravi: Can People Ops provide anonymized appeal rates and overturn counts from last two cycles? Leadership wants to know how often panels change outcomes.

amy: Yes  I will pull anonymized stats (counts and overturn %) and post here within 48 hours. No PII, just org-level/level-level breakdowns if requested.

zara: One more: any change to benefits or comp-related policy this cycle? Someone mentioned the 401k match cliff change in the all-hands.

amy: The 401k match cadence is unchanged for this cycle; HR will announce any future benefit policy changes separately. For comp policy changes that affect eligibility we will publish a policy diff doc alongside the timeline.

bryan: Thanks Amy. Could we get a short manager office hour to run through the appeal form and band-only moves? Some new managers would appreciate a walkthrough.

amy: Yes  scheduling a 45-min office hour tomorrow 10:00 PT for managers doing calibrations & appeals. Zoom link + calendar invite will be posted here shortly. Ping me if you need a different time. :calendar:

peopleops-bot: Calendar invite posted: "Manager calibration & appeals office hour" 2026-05-19 17:00 UTC. :spiral_calendar_pad:

amy: Thanks all. I'll add the anonymized metrics, the appeal form link, and the band-move template to this thread when ready. Drop any follow-ups here and I'll triage. :raised_hands:
